body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (1) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Superseded holds can still permit merges 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>check_sensitive accepts a trusted decision after a matching hold without checking whether that
>decision says the hold was superseded, despite the new instruction to post clearing decisions that
>allow nothing. If a newer hold follows only review-record changes, the older hold still passes the
>head check, so supplying its clearing decision to gate or merge --allow-hold 5 permits the
>merge.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[ARCHITECT.md[366]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/16/files#diff-ea2e7d73022c92135dc25cc66e267892824f32ecb823bb758697588c630d9cc1R366-R366) > >```diff >+Every hold ends with `head `, the PR head it showed. When several holds for one PR are open, answer the newest. Before Matthew decides it, show him what changed on its held paths since the older hold, in a clone of the repo (5.3 step 1): `git fetch origin pull//head`, then `git diff -- `. An empty diff means the same code. Clear each older hold at the same sitting (step 7) with a `DECISION` that allows nothing ("superseded by MERGE-HOLD-"). The gate refuses an older hold's decision at a newer head anyway. >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>Semantic gap: gate can't read a decision's wording; no close accept or reject precedent. Team
>tightened this hold/decision pairing before (PR #7), but the review-record-only case is by design.
>
> > [PR-#7](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/7) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The added workflow explicitly calls for a DECISION that allows nothing for each older hold. The
>gate queries holds by the supplied decision number and pairs any fresh same-number hold with a later
>trusted decision; it does not inspect newer holds or the decision's permission. A head remains fresh
>when intervening paths are all exempt review records, as the new test also demonstrates.
>
> > [ARCHITECT.md\[364-366\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/d9722dd16c67573f47c9e7f8d2e9aaf5273d1576/ARCHITECT.md/#L364-L366) > [room.py\[2516-2530\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/d9722dd16c67573f47c9e7f8d2e9aaf5273d1576/room.py/#L2516-L2530) > [room.py\[2563-2573\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/d9722dd16c67573f47c9e7f8d2e9aaf5273d1576/room.py/#L2563-L2573) > [tests/test_m6f.py\[129-143\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/d9722dd16c67573f47c9e7f8d2e9aaf5273d1576/tests/test_m6f.py/#L129-L143) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The new multi-hold workflow creates clearing decisions for older holds, but the gate can treat those decisions as merge authorization when only review records changed. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- ARCHITECT.md[366-366] >- room.py[2563-2573] > >## Recommended Fix >Make the gate reject an older hold's decision once a newer hold for the same PR supersedes it, while preserving the existing allowance for review-record-only changes after a hold that has not been superseded. Test a newer review-record-only hold followed by an older clearing decision, and remove or qualify the documentation's unconditional refusal claim. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c9be4e47-fcd9-4321-ace0-834ae7359e70?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/c9be4e47-fcd9-4321-ace0-834ae7359e70)

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
